questions.q: What did Sune Lehmann's study of attention find?
a: Cultural trends have been getting shorter for about two centuries
Attention spans only began shrinking with the smartphone
Book reading has fallen steadily since the 1950s
People now recall fewer facts than they did a decade ago
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the rise and fall of popular books over 200 years shows trend cycles shortening before the internet.

questions.q: How long did the average trending topic last on Twitter after the 2013 to 2016 decline?
a: Just over 11 hours, down from over 17
Just over 7 hours, down from over 11
Just over 17 hours, down from over 24
Just over 20 hours, down from over 30
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the average duration of a trending topic fell by more than 30%, from over 17 hours to just over 11.

questions.q: Why does the summary call free social media expensive?
a: Users pay for it with their time and attention
It quietly charges a monthly subscription fee
It sells users' private messages to advertisers
It requires expensive devices to access
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the real price of free platforms is the time and attention they capture.

questions.q: What did a 2020 Wall Street Journal report reveal about Facebook?
a: It knew its algorithms exploited people's attraction to divisiveness
It had decided to ban political advertising entirely
It was losing money on its main news feed
It planned to start charging users for verification
questions.why: Lesson 2 quotes an internal presentation admitting the algorithms exploit the brain's pull toward divisiveness.

questions.q: Which mental state does the summary recommend practicing instead of multitasking?
a: Flow, losing yourself in a task and losing track of time
Deep work, blocking out every distraction for four hours
Mindfulness, watching your thoughts without judging them
Batching, grouping similar tasks into a single block
questions.why: Lesson 3 recommends single-tasking and describes flow as the state where time disappears.
